title: Tractor FC Ticket Sales Platform
tagline: A NestJS microservice powering the Tractor Club stadium ticketing platform.
description: A modular NestJS microservice that powers the ticketing platform for Tractor Club stadium events. It manages the full lifecycle of stadium inventory and ticketing: stadiums, zones, sections, seats, gates, matches, seat reservations with Redis-backed bitmap locking, ticket issuance, payments, KYC, provider discounts, waiting lists, and attendee check-in.

details.overview: A modular NestJS microservice powering the ticketing platform for Tractor Club stadium events. It manages the complete stadium ticketing lifecycle, including stadium inventory (zones, sections, seats, and gates), match scheduling, high-concurrency seat reservations using Redis-backed bitmap locking and atomic Lua scripts, ticket issuance, payment verification, attendee KYC and check-in, provider discounts, waiting lists, and notifications. The service exposes a versioned REST API with Swagger documentation, health checks, structured Pino logging, and optional RabbitMQ messaging.
responsibilities: Designed and implemented modular NestJS modules for stadium inventory, matches, reservations, tickets, payments, and attendees.
Implemented Redis-backed bitmap seat locking with atomic Lua scripts for high-concurrency seat selection.
Integrated PostgreSQL via TypeORM with migrations and Redis (single node or Sentinel).
Built payment initiation/verification, refunds, and HMAC-protected provider discounts.
Implemented KYC identity verification and external stadium ticketing service integration.
Added waiting list, attendee gate check-in, notifications, and optional RabbitMQ publisher/consumer subsystem.
Configured i18n (Persian default), JWT auth, Swagger docs, health checks, and Cockatiel resilience (timeout, retry, circuit breaker).

technicalChallenges.title: High-Concurrency Seat Reservation
technicalChallenges.problem: Multiple requests could attempt to reserve the same seat simultaneously.
technicalChallenges.approach: Used Redis-backed bitmap seat locking with atomic Lua scripts to guarantee atomic, race-free seat selection under high concurrency.

technicalChallenges.title: Stadium Inventory Hierarchy
technicalChallenges.problem: Modeling stadiums, zones, platforms, sections, and seats with consistent propagation and seat counts.
technicalChallenges.approach: Implemented hierarchy resolver and propagation services to keep inventory counts consistent across the stadium hierarchy.

technicalChallenges.title: Resilience to Upstream Failures
technicalChallenges.problem: Upstream services (KYC, Jaberi, payments, notifications) may be slow or unavailable.
technicalChallenges.approach: Applied Cockatiel policies (timeout, retry, circuit breaker) around HTTP clients to degrade gracefully.

architecture.description: A modular NestJS service organized into feature modules (Stadium, Zone, Platform, Section, Seat, Gate, Match, MatchStadium, Attendee, Reservation, ProviderDiscount, Ticket, Payment, Kyc, Jaberi, User, WaitingList, Notification, Health) over shared core infrastructure (config, database, files, logger, resilience) and common cross-cutting concerns (filters, interceptors, pipes, guards, interfaces). PostgreSQL via TypeORM is the primary data store, Redis provides caching and atomic seat locking, and RabbitMQ is an optional messaging layer. External integrations include KYC, Jaberi, payment gateway, and notification service.

title: KYC Identity Verification Service
tagline: A NestJS microservice for Know Your Customer (KYC) identity verification with pluggable provider strategies.
description: A NestJS microservice that provides Know Your Customer (KYC) identity verification. It exposes three API surfaces — internal service (/api/v1/service/kyc), end-user (/api/v1/user/kyc), and admin (/api/v1/admin) — each protected by dedicated guards and gateway-injected authentication. Verifications run synchronously via async/await with pluggable provider strategies and automatic priority-based fallback (UID, Jibit). Features include Fancard KYC, short-circuit verification of already-verified steps, per-provider resilience policies (retry, timeout, circuit breaker via Cockatiel), a subject data model storing full identity profiles, event-driven audit logging and user-service webhook callbacks, an under-18 guardian OTP flow, Sub-KYC (verifying on behalf of another user), TypeORM migrations with PostgreSQL, AWS S3 document uploads, structured Pino logging, i18n (fa/en), and Swagger UI at /api/docs.

details.overview: A NestJS microservice providing KYC identity verification for Tractor Club platforms. It exposes three authenticated API surfaces for internal services, end users, and administrators, and processes verifications synchronously through a pluggable provider pipeline with priority-based fallback between UID and Jibit. The service manages identity profiles, multiple verification types and statuses, Fancard verification with admin manual review, under-18 guardian OTP flows, and Sub-KYC verification on behalf of other users. It also supports provider credential management, resilient provider integrations with retries, timeouts, and circuit breakers via Cockatiel, AWS S3 document uploads, event-driven audit logging, user-service webhook callbacks, health checks, and internationalization (Persian and English). Built with PostgreSQL and TypeORM migrations, structured Pino logging, dedicated authentication guards, and Swagger API documentation.
responsibilities: Designed and implemented modular NestJS modules for KYC verification, subject management, provider management, audit, events, health, and settings.
Built a synchronous verification pipeline with pluggable provider strategies and priority-based fallback (UID, Jibit).
Applied Cockatiel resilience policies (retry, timeout, circuit breaker) around provider HTTP clients for graceful degradation.
Implemented Fancard KYC, under-18 guardian OTP verification flow, and Sub-KYC (verifying on behalf of another user).
Integrated AWS S3 for KYC document uploads (images, videos, PDFs) with presigned URLs.
Configured three API surfaces with gateway-injected authentication: UserInfoGuard, AdminRoleGuard, and ServiceAuthDecorator.
Added event-driven audit logging and user-service webhook callbacks for verification state changes.
Set up TypeORM migrations with PostgreSQL, Pino structured JSON logging, Swagger docs, i18n (Persian default), and health checks.

features.title: Resilience Policies
features.description: Per-provider Cockatiel policies: retry, timeout, and circuit breaker to degrade gracefully under upstream failures.

features.title: Subject Data Model
features.description: Stores a full identity profile per user reference, including verification levels and dates.

features.title: Fancard KYC
features.description: Internal fan-card verification with no external provider — males auto-verified, females require admin review.

features.title: Under-18 Guardian OTP Flow
features.description: Guardian OTP delivery with 30-second cooldown, up to three resends within 15 minutes, and requested-info prefill without leaking the OTP.

features.title: Sub-KYC
features.description: One user can initiate verification on behalf of another subject.

features.title: Admin Manual Review
features.description: Admin endpoints to list, review, approve, or reject Fancard and Foreign Fancard verifications awaiting manual review.

features.title: Provider Management
features.description: Admin CRUD for KYC providers and provider priorities, including encrypted credential storage at rest.

features.title: S3 Document Uploads
features.description: Upload KYC documents (images, videos, PDFs) to AWS S3 with presigned URL support.

features.title: Observability
features.description: Structured Pino JSON logging, Swagger UI at /api/docs, i18n (Persian default), and public health checks (database, memory, disk).

technicalChallenges.title: Provider Failover & Resilience
technicalChallenges.problem: Upstream KYC providers (UID, Jibit) may be slow or unavailable, risking failed verifications.
technicalChallenges.approach: Applied Cockatiel resilience policies (retry, timeout, circuit breaker) around each provider HTTP client, with priority-based automatic fallback to a secondary provider.

technicalChallenges.title: Synchronous Multi-Step Verification
technicalChallenges.problem: Coordinating several verification steps in order while skipping steps that are already verified.
technicalChallenges.approach: Implemented a synchronous pipeline using direct async/await with short-circuit logic that skips already-verified steps and surfaces the first blocking or failed step.

technicalChallenges.title: Three Distinct Auth Surfaces
technicalChallenges.problem: Service, user, and admin endpoints require different authentication models and role checks.
technicalChallenges.approach: Created dedicated guards (ServiceAuthDecorator, UserInfoGuard, AdminRoleGuard) and applied them per route group so each surface enforces its own auth contract.

technicalChallenges.title: Sensitive Data Protection
technicalChallenges.problem: Provider credentials and subject PII must be encrypted at rest.
technicalChallenges.approach: Used an AES encryption transformer (PROVIDER_ENCRYPTION_KEY) to encrypt provider credentials and subject data before persisting to PostgreSQL.

technicalChallenges.title: Under-18 Guardian OTP Flow
technicalChallenges.problem: Guardian OTP must be delivered, rate-limited, and never leaked to the client, while still allowing form prefill.
technicalChallenges.approach: Tracked OTP state server-side with a 30-second cooldown, a three-resend limit within 15 minutes, and exposed only requestedInfo (never the OTP) for client prefill.

architecture.description: A modular NestJS service organized into feature modules (Kyc, Subject, ProviderManagement, Health, Audit, Events, Settings) over shared core infrastructure (config, database, redis, logger, resilience, observability, swagger) and common cross-cutting concerns (filters, interceptors, pipes, guards, decorators, dto, enums, interfaces, utils). Integrations include UID and Jibit KYC providers, AWS S3 file storage, and notification/webhook delivery. PostgreSQL via TypeORM is the primary data store, Redis provides caching and rate limiting, and Cockatiel resilience policies wrap provider HTTP clients. Three API surfaces (/api/v1/service/kyc, /api/v1/user/kyc, /api/v1/admin) are each protected by dedicated guards. The verification pipeline runs synchronously via async/await with pluggable provider strategies, priority-based fallback, and short-circuiting of already-verified steps. Event-driven side effects emit audit logs and user-service webhook callbacks.

title: Content Management API
tagline: A NestJS backend for managing multi-language news, galleries, matches, and media for Tractor FC.
description: A production-ready NestJS backend that powers the Tractor FC landing platform. It manages multi-language news content (English/Persian) with tagging, SEO-friendly slugs, scheduled publishing, featured ordering, and full-text search across MongoDB and Elasticsearch. It also handles galleries, match data with live overlays and head-to-head stats, ads, ticketing subsystems, analytics/view tracking, file management with AWS S3, and event-driven side effects via RabbitMQ. Includes JWT auth, Sentry observability, Swagger docs, and Docker deployment.

details.overview: A production-ready NestJS backend powering the Tractor FC content and landing platform. It exposes REST APIs for multilingual news (English/Persian), tags, galleries, match data, advertisements, ticketing, and file management. Features include SEO-friendly slugs, scheduled publishing, featured content ordering, full-text search, live match overlays, head-to-head statistics, and analytics with view tracking. The service integrates MongoDB for primary data storage, Elasticsearch for search, Redis for caching and rate limiting, RabbitMQ for event-driven processing, and AWS S3 for media storage and management. Additional capabilities include JWT authentication, Sentry error monitoring, Swagger API documentation, and Docker-based deployment.
responsibilities: Designed and implemented the file manager subsystem with AWS S3 uploads, Sharp-based image processing, dynamic watermarking, multi-quality (high/low) generation, WebP conversion, and file count limits.
Implemented Elasticsearch integration for news search: mappings, ngram tokenizers, atomic view-count increments, and sync pipelines with transactional outbox delivery.
Built analytics features including reusable visitor-ID middleware for daily view deduplication and queued Redis view-sync cron jobs.
Developed match features: live overlays, head-to-head match APIs, and related news conditions.
Implemented scheduled news publishing with transactional outbox and RabbitMQ event publishing for news and gallery updates.
Added marquee generation for news and galleries from RabbitMQ events and notification triggers on gallery updates.
Integrated Sentry error monitoring and APM, structured logging, and Docker-based deployment.
Maintained Mongoose schemas, indexes, and seeders; hardened Redis sync and Elasticsearch error handling.

technicalChallenges.problem: Generating watermarked, compressed, multi-quality images at scale without degrading performance.
technicalChallenges.approach: Used Sharp with dynamic watermark scaling/margins, WebP conversion for low quality, and S3-backed high-quality migration APIs.

technicalChallenges.title: Search Relevance
technicalChallenges.problem: Providing accurate multi-language full-text search with substring matching.
technicalChallenges.approach: Centralized Elasticsearch config with ngram tokenizers, env-driven index names, and atomic view-count increments.

technicalChallenges.title: Reliable Event Delivery

technicalChallenges.approach: Implemented transactional outbox pattern with scheduled delivery and RabbitMQ integration.

technicalChallenges.approach: Reusable visitor-ID middleware with queued async Redis sync cron and atomic Elasticsearch increments.

title: Short Link Generator Service API
tagline: A high-performance URL shortener service with a web UI, REST API, Redis caching, and Docker deployment for Tractor marketing.
description: A Node.js/Express URL shortener service built for Tractor marketing. It converts long URLs into short, shareable links with optional custom aliases, tracks click counts, and resolves short URLs with a Redis-first caching layer backed by MongoDB. It ships a web interface (EJS) plus a REST API, HMAC-authenticated client endpoints, an admin page with recent-link management, redirect animations, ads integration, health monitoring, MongoDB weekly backups, and Nginx/Docker deployment. The service is containerized with MongoDB 7 and Redis 7 via Docker Compose.

card.imageAlt: Short Link Generator Service API cover

details.overview: A URL shortener service for Tractor marketing, built with Node.js and Express, persisting mappings in MongoDB and caching them in Redis for fast resolution. It exposes both a browser UI and a REST API, supports custom aliases and click tracking. Features include HMAC client authentication, an admin page, redirect animations, ads integration, health endpoint, and automated MongoDB backups.
responsibilities: Built the core URL shortening flow: validation, unique short ID generation (nanoid), optional custom aliases, MongoDB persistence, and Redis caching.
Implemented fast URL resolution with Redis-first lookup, MongoDB fallback, click-count updates in both stores, and redirect handling.
Added custom alias support with alphanumeric validation and uniqueness checks.
Built the web interface (EJS) for creating short links and an admin page listing recently created links, moved to client-side cookies.
Added redirect animations and pre-load page for a smoother redirect experience.
Implemented HMAC-based authentication for API clients and client examples.
Added health endpoint for uptime monitoring and removed Elastic APM instrumentation.
Added ads API integration and banners on error pages.
Restricted API-domain access to API endpoints only and refactored Nginx URL access.
Added MongoDB weekly backup scripts and Docker/Nginx deployment configuration.
Fixed redirect bugs and the duplicate-short-link generation bug for identical long URLs.
Updated generated link styling and copy options in the admin UI.

technicalChallenges.title: Fast URL Resolution
technicalChallenges.problem: Short-link redirects must be low-latency even under load.
technicalChallenges.approach: Redis-first lookup with MongoDB fallback, updating click counts in both stores.

technicalChallenges.title: Duplicate Link Prevention
technicalChallenges.problem: The same long URL could generate different short links.
technicalChallenges.approach: Fixed generation logic to reuse existing mappings for identical long URLs.

technicalChallenges.title: Custom Alias Uniqueness
technicalChallenges.problem: Custom aliases must be alphanumeric and unique.
technicalChallenges.approach: Validated aliases with valid-url/alphanumeric rules and enforced uniqueness in MongoDB.

technicalChallenges.title: Client-Side Recent Links
technicalChallenges.problem: Server-stored recent links table was unnecessary overhead.
technicalChallenges.approach: Moved recent created links to client cookies and removed the server table.

architecture.description: Express.js application (app.js) with routes for shortening, redirect, health, and admin. MongoDB (Mongoose) persists URL mappings; Redis caches mappings keyed by shorturl:{BASE_URL}/{shortID} for fast resolution. EJS renders the web UI and admin page. Nginx fronts the app and restricts API-domain access to API endpoints. Docker Compose orchestrates the Node app, MongoDB 7, and Redis 7. HMAC auth secures API clients; automated scripts handle MongoDB weekly backups.

title: Daric Holding Backend Platform
tagline: A two-part NestJS backend system powering the Daric Holding group — an admin panel API and a public website backend API working together.
description: The Daric Holding Backend Platform is a complete NestJS backend system for the Daric Holding group, composed of two cooperating parts: the Daric Holding Admin Panel API and the Daric Holding Website Backend API. Together they form a full content and hiring management system. The Admin Panel API handles authenticated admin operations — users, roles, granular permission-based access control, hiring panel (job opportunities, work domains, job applications, employment applications with resume/photo uploads and Excel export), organizational chart management, contact requests with email notifications, publication workflow (draft/published/archived), and file management. The Website Backend API serves the public-facing website — homepage sections (activities, companies, holdings, search, founder biography, activity areas, latest events, latest projects, settings/social media), public hiring APIs matching the frontend mock data format, organizational charts, history content, and file/asset serving. The two parts work together: the admin panel publishes content that the website backend consumes and exposes to the frontend. Built with TypeScript, MongoDB/Mongoose, Swagger-documented REST APIs, nestjs-i18n (Persian fallback), JWT auth, and Docker.

details.overview: A complete NestJS backend platform for the Daric Holding group, split into two cooperating repositories: an Admin Panel API (darik-api) and a Website Backend API (daric-holding-backend-web). The admin panel manages users, roles, permissions, hiring workflows (job opportunities, work domains, job applications, employment applications with file uploads and Excel export), organizational charts, contact requests with email notifications, publication status control, and file management. The website backend serves public homepage data, hiring APIs compatible with the frontend mock data, org charts, history content, and static assets. Published content flows from the admin panel to the website backend, which exposes it to the website frontend. Both use MongoDB, TypeScript, Swagger, and nestjs-i18n with Persian fallback.
responsibilities: Implemented granular permission-based access control with Permission and Role modules, including role assignment and authorization guards; fixed permission guard and refactored permissions/authorization access to APIs.
Implemented the hiring module: job opportunities, work domains, job applications, and employment applications with panel review and email notification on both admin panel and website backend.
Added Excel export for employment applications including resume and photo data; fixed Excel missing data and email data styling.

Implemented employment application V2 with resume/photo file uploads, preventing duplicate applications using national code; unified application submission with file uploads and fixed uploaded file URL handling.

Implemented company-chart module: employee creation with validation, organizational chart mock data, pagination, child reordering for hierarchy display, and chart data on position; exposed org chart to both admin panel and website.
Implemented contact-us module with email notifications for contact requests, settings-based recipient, MJML email templates, and RTL support.

Implemented homepage module APIs: first section (activities, companies, holdings), featured section, search bar by faName, founder info biography, activity area, latest events, latest projects, and settings/social media endpoints.
Built public hiring website APIs matching the exact frontend mock data format: job opportunities with filtering/pagination, work domains, companies, cities, and job applications.
Removed admin panel APIs from the website application to separate public and admin concerns; refactored environment configuration and removed ESLint config.
Supported publication management (draft/published/archived) for hiring and history content; website APIs return only published content while panel APIs show all content.

Managed Git workflows: merging feature branches (hiring, employee-hiring, contact-us-email, role-management) into development and main; bugfix/hiring-excel merges; updating env files and adding missing variables.

title: AI Shell
tagline: A local-first AI assistant for your Zsh shell, powered by Ollama.
description: AI Shell (`ai`) is a local-first AI assistant for the Zsh shell. It is a small Go program that talks to a locally-running Ollama instance for inference and an optional, self-managed SearXNG container for web search. There is no cloud dependency, no paid API, and no telemetry — everything runs on your machine. It is used as a shell function that captures terminal context (current directory, previous command, exit code, git status) and feeds it to the model, so questions like "why did that fail?" just work. Responses stream back as they are generated, conversation history is kept per shell session, and the assistant can optionally suggest (and, with confirmation, execute) shell commands with risk-tier classification and an audit log.

card.imageAlt: AI Shell terminal banner describing its local-first Zsh assistant features

details.overview: A local-first AI assistant for Zsh built as a single Go binary with two run modes (client and daemon) communicating over a Unix domain socket. The daemon owns the Ollama connection, per-session chat memory, and an optional SearXNG container. It provides streaming answers, Markdown rendering in the terminal, terminal-context injection, model profile management (add/remove/switch at runtime), optional web search via a self-managed SearXNG container, and optional command execution with risk tiers and confirmation. Configuration lives in YAML and is created by a first-run wizard with GPU-aware preflight checks.
responsibilities: Designed and implemented the entire Go codebase from scratch as the sole developer.
Built the client/daemon architecture: a single `ai` binary that lazily spawns a background daemon over a Unix domain socket and speaks a newline-delimited JSON protocol.
Implemented the Ollama HTTP client with streaming `/api/generate` and `/api/tags` support.
Created the config system: YAML load/save with defaults, model profiles, first-run wizard, and runtime add/remove of model profiles persisted to config.
Built preflight checks: Ollama/GPU detection, VRAM-aware context-length suggestions, guided model pulling, and first-run setup.
Implemented terminal context injection: captures cwd, last command, exit code, and git status from Zsh and feeds them into the model's system prompt.
Built per-session in-memory chat state with capped history and pending-suggestion handling.
Implemented optional web search: a basic function-calling loop where the model can request a SearXNG search, plus a SearXNG client and container lifecycle manager (Docker).

Implemented optional command execution: structured JSON suggestions (`{explanation, commands, risk}`), glob-based risk classification (low/medium/high), user confirmation (typed `yes` for high risk), execution via `sh -c`, and an audit log.
Wrote a tiny dependency-free ANSI Markdown renderer and markdown detection for TTY output.
Wrote the Zsh shell function (`ai.zsh`) for integration, including session-token capture and context forwarding via environment variables.
Added the `help` command, `model`/`models`/`model-add`/`model-rm` subcommands, and `--model` one-off override.
Wrote unit tests for every package (`go test ./...`) and documentation (README, architecture, configuration, web-search guides).

features.title: Local inference only
features.description: All chats go to Ollama on localhost; nothing leaves your machine, no cloud dependency, no paid API, no telemetry.

features.title: Streaming answers
features.description: Tokens are printed as they arrive from Ollama through the daemon to the client in real time.

features.title: Markdown rendering
features.description: Answers are re-rendered as ANSI-styled Markdown in the terminal (disabled automatically when output is piped).

features.title: Terminal context
features.description: The Zsh function captures cwd, previous command, exit code, and git status and feeds them to the model.

features.title: Session memory
features.description: Short conversation history kept per shell session (in-memory, capped, not persisted).

features.title: Model switching
features.description: Switch the active model per shell, list configured profiles, or override for a single query; add/remove profiles at runtime.

features.title: Optional web search
features.description: AI Shell manages its own SearXNG container and uses it only when the model decides a query needs live information.

features.title: Optional command execution
features.description: The assistant suggests shell commands with a risk tier and runs them after confirmation, logging every executed command.

features.title: First-run wizard & preflight
features.description: GPU-aware Ollama install guidance, VRAM detection, model pulling, and interactive config creation.

technicalChallenges.title: Client/daemon socket protocol
technicalChallenges.problem: The CLI must remain a short-lived process while the daemon holds long-lived state (Ollama connection, sessions). They needed a robust, language-agnostic IPC mechanism.
technicalChallenges.approach: Used Unix domain sockets with newline-delimited JSON request/response types (query, model_switch, model_list, model_add, model_remove, execute_confirm, and chunk/searching/notice/done/error responses). The client auto-spawns the daemon when the socket is unreachable.

technicalChallenges.title: Streaming with Markdown re-rendering
technicalChallenges.problem: Ollama tokens should stream live, but Markdown needs the full answer to render nicely on a TTY.
technicalChallenges.approach: Print chunks verbatim while they arrive, buffer them, then on completion jump the cursor back and replace the plain text with ANSI-styled Markdown — only when rendering is enabled, stdout is a TTY, and the content looks like Markdown.

technicalChallenges.title: Safe optional command execution
technicalChallenges.problem: Letting an AI suggest shell commands is dangerous; commands must never run silently and high-risk actions need strong confirmation.
technicalChallenges.approach: The model returns structured JSON (`{explanation, commands, risk}`); risk is classified from config globs; every command is shown and confirmed before running (high risk requires typing `yes`); every run is logged to an audit file.

technicalChallenges.title: Isolating Docker usage
technicalChallenges.problem: Web search needs a SearXNG container managed by Docker, but the rest of the codebase should not shell out to Docker.
technicalChallenges.approach: Split into `internal/web` (a pure HTTP client for an already-running SearXNG instance) and `internal/searxng` (owns the container lifecycle via `os/exec`). All Docker usage lives in the latter.

technicalChallenges.title: Minimal dependency footprint
technicalChallenges.problem: Keeping the binary small and auditable without pulling in CLI frameworks, routers, ORMs, or UUID libraries.
technicalChallenges.approach: Standard library only plus `gopkg.in/yaml.v3`; hand-rolled glob-to-regexp compiler for risk rules and a small ANSI Markdown writer.

architecture.description: AI Shell is a single Go binary (`ai`) with two run modes over a Unix domain socket. `cmd/ai/main.go` is the entrypoint: `ai daemon` runs preflight and serves the socket; everything else is client mode, which ensures the daemon is running (spawning it if needed), dials the socket, sends a JSON request, and streams responses back. The Zsh function (`ai.zsh`) calls the binary as the client, injecting context via environment variables. Internal packages: `config` (YAML load/save/defaults), `preflight` (Ollama/GPU checks, model pulling, first-run wizard, SearXNG setup), `ollama` (HTTP client for Ollama's `/api/generate` streaming + `/api/tags`, `ollama pull`), `daemon` (Unix socket server, JSON protocol, request routing, web tool loop), `session` (in-memory per-session chat state + pending suggestion), `context` (gather cwd/git/last-command/exit-code into a system prompt), `execution` (structured suggestions, risk classification, confirmation, execution, audit log), `web` (pure SearXNG HTTP client), `searxng` (manages the SearXNG container lifecycle via Docker), and `markdown` (tiny dependency-free ANSI Markdown renderer). Startup runs preflight (Ollama reachability, GPU/VRAM detection, wizard, model pulls, optional SearXNG container), then opens the daemon log, builds the Ollama client, and serves the socket. Query handling resolves the model, optionally runs the web-search decision loop against SearXNG, then branches to chat (streamed answer) or execution (JSON suggestion, risk classify, confirm, run). Sessions live in a mutex-guarded map capped by `max_history_messages`; state is in-memory only and tied to the shell.

title: Kanban Board
tagline: A lightweight VS Code extension for managing Markdown-based Kanban boards.
description: Kanban Board is a VS Code extension that transforms Markdown files into interactive Kanban boards. Each level-2 heading becomes a column and each checklist item becomes a draggable task. It provides full two-way synchronization between the visual board and the underlying Markdown file, with support for priorities, notes, comments, column reordering, cross-board task movement, keyboard shortcuts, and theme switching

card.imageAlt: Kanban Board extension interface showing tasks in columns

details.overview: A VS Code extension that renders Markdown files as interactive Kanban boards. The extension parses `##` headings as columns and `- [ ]`/`- [x]` checklist items as tasks, maintains stable UUIDs for tasks, and writes all changes back to Markdown. Features include drag-and-drop, task priorities, multi-line notes, comments, cross-board movement, column reordering, find/search, keyboard shortcuts, and dark/light themes. Built with TypeScript and the VS Code Webview API.
responsibilities: Designed and implemented the entire VS Code extension from scratch as the sole developer.
Built the Markdown parser to read/write tasks with columns, priorities, notes, comments, and stable IDs.
Implemented the Kanban logic layer for task operations (add/move/toggle/remove), column management, and cross-board task movement.
Created the VS Code extension entry point with commands to open boards from workspace or from any Markdown file.
Developed the webview UI with drag-and-drop, modals for task details/comments, column reordering, and keyboard interactions.
Implemented two-way sync between the webview and Markdown files with automatic ID generation for tasks.
Added file watching for external changes with auto-refresh of open panels.
Built task priority system (5 levels), comments serialization in task lines, and multi-line note support.
Implemented keyboard shortcuts and chord commands (Ctrl/Cmd+G then Ctrl/Cmd+T).
Added dark/light theme toggle with persistence and RTL/LTR text detection.
Created test suite with Mocha for parser and kanban logic.
Released versions 0.1.0 through 0.4.0 with continuous feature additions and improvements.

technicalChallenges.title: Two-way Markdown synchronization
technicalChallenges.problem: Keeping the visual Kanban board in sync with Markdown files while preserving formatting like notes (indented), comments, and IDs.
technicalChallenges.approach: Built a custom Markdown parser that reads `##` sections and checkbox items, extracts metadata from inline tags like `[id:...]`, `[Priority:...]`, `[Comments:...]`, and parses indented lines as notes. Writer serializes back in a consistent format with 4-space indentation for notes.

technicalChallenges.title: Cross-board task movement
technicalChallenges.problem: Moving tasks between different Markdown files while maintaining data integrity and refreshing all open panels.
technicalChallenges.approach: Implemented `moveTaskBetweenFiles` in the kanban module that reads source, removes task by ID, inserts into target at specified position, writes both files. Extension tracks all open panels by file path and refreshes them after cross-board moves.

technicalChallenges.title: Webview state management
technicalChallenges.problem: Managing multiple Kanban instances for different files, handling drag-and-drop across boards, and keeping UI in sync with file changes.
technicalChallenges.approach: Used VS Code Webview API with message passing between extension host and webview. Each panel has its own Kanban instance. Implemented file watching with debouncing to auto-refresh on external changes. Tracked panels in a Map by file path.

technicalChallenges.title: Rich task metadata in Markdown
technicalChallenges.problem: Storing priorities, comments, IDs, and notes in a human-readable Markdown format without breaking existing tools.
technicalChallenges.approach: Encoded metadata as inline tags in task lines (`[id: uuid] [Priority: High] [Comments: a | b]`) and used indentation for multi-line notes. Parser handles these tags robustly with regex, writer serializes consistently.

technicalChallenges.title: Stable task identity
technicalChallenges.problem: Enabling reliable task movement and updates even if text changes.
technicalChallenges.approach: Assigned each task a stable UUID via `crypto.randomUUID()`, stored as `[id: ...]`, auto-generated on read if missing and persisted back to file. All operations use IDs for cross-board moves.

architecture.description: VS Code extension architecture with three main layers: Extension Host (TypeScript) handling VS Code API integration, Kanban/Parser logic for Markdown processing, and Webview UI (HTML/CSS/JS) for the board interface. The extension registers commands, manages webview panels per file, watches files for changes, and communicates via postMessage. The parser reads/writes Markdown with column/task/note/comment/ID parsing. The Kanban class provides high-level operations and persists changes immediately.

title: Nest Craft
tagline: A batteries-included CLI for scaffolding and enhancing production-ready NestJS projects.
description: Nest Craft is a Node.js CLI tool that streamlines creating and evolving NestJS applications. It orchestrates `nest new`, applies opinionated defaults (ConfigModule and env files, ESLint/Prettier/Jest tweaks, typed env/request definitions, static assets), and can inject production-focused features into both new and existing NestJS codebases through interactive, cancellation-safe prompts. The generator can wire API prefixing and URI versioning, security middleware (CORS, Helmet, custom headers), validation/interceptors/filters, Swagger with custom UI assets, pagination utilities for TypeORM or Mongoose, Multer upload helpers, Winston-based logging with request context, and a Docker Compose setup with selectable services, custom networks, and smart dependencies.

card.imageAlt: Nest Craft terminal prompt framed by a woven nest-inspired emblem

details.overview: Nest Craft is a globally installable CLI (`nest-craft`) that helps developers bootstrap real-world NestJS projects and retrofit features into existing repositories. The interactive workflow supports multiple package managers (npm, yarn, pnpm), optional Git initialization, Docker service selection, and feature toggles. Under the hood it shells out to `@nestjs/cli` for base project creation, copies curated templates/configs into the target app, installs required dependencies, and patches `src/main.ts` and project configuration to enable selected capabilities (API prefix/versioning, validation, security, Swagger, logging, pagination, uploads, and more). An `--add-feature` mode re-runs feature injection against an existing NestJS project, while `--list-features`, `--help`, and `--version` provide discoverability and CLI ergonomics.
responsibilities: Designed and implemented the Nest Craft CLI from the initial release (v1.0.0) through subsequent feature releases, based on commit history for saeednorouzi98@gmail.com
Built the command-line entrypoint and argument routing (`init`, `--add-feature`, `--list-features`, `--help`, `--version`) and the interactive initialization/add-feature workflows.

Implemented project scaffolding orchestration around `@nestjs/cli` and shell execution, including package-manager support, directory setup, app module handling, and non-sudo/permission/error-handling guard rails.

Created the Docker Compose generator with selectable services, service-specific config drops (e.g., Dockerfile/nginx.conf), custom network validation, and dynamic `depends_on` wiring for the Node service.
Developed template and file-management systems to seed configs, typed definitions, Swagger assets, pagination/Multer utilities, security modules, and Winston logger components into target projects.

Implemented `main.ts` modification logic to register selected global features (prefix, URI versioning, pipes, filters, interceptors, CORS/Helmet, static assets, Swagger, Winston logger wiring) with safe bootstrap handling.

Added and refined features across releases: `--add-feature` retrofit flow, global API prefix/versioning prompts, security utilities (CORS/Helmet/fake tech-stack headers), pagination DTO/interface/driver utilities, Multer module refactor, and Winston Logger integration (v1.5.0).
Improved Swagger UX and configuration (custom UI assets, styling/scripts, config updates) and fixed/refined CORS, pagination, and logger setup behavior in later maintenance commits.
Maintained project documentation and release history (`README.md`, `LOGS.md`) alongside version bumps and feature announcements.

features.title: Interactive Project Scaffolding

features.title: Feature Injection for Existing Projects
features.description: `--add-feature` validates a target NestJS project and applies selected features/configs (including Docker Compose generation) without re-scaffolding the whole app.

features.title: Docker Compose Generator
features.description: Generates `docker-compose.yml` from selectable services (Node, databases, caches, brokers, search, admin tools, Nginx, etc.) with optional custom networks, smart `depends_on`, and service-specific config file drops.

features.title: Main.ts & App Wiring Automation
features.description: Patches `src/main.ts` to enable selected capabilities such as `NestExpressApplication`, static assets, global prefix, URI API versioning, validation, filters, interceptors, CORS/Helmet, Swagger, and Winston logger integration.

features.title: Security Utilities
features.description: Provides prompt-driven security options including reusable CORS config, opinionated Helmet setup, and a custom headers interceptor to spoof tech-stack headers.

features.title: Swagger Integration with Custom UI

features.title: Pagination & File Upload Toolkits
features.description: Ships pagination DTO/interface/utilities for TypeORM and Mongoose, and a Multer module with typed config/utilities and upload/file cleanup helpers under `assets`.

features.title: Winston Logger Module
features.description: Adds a production-oriented logger setup with NestJS `LoggerService` integration, request-context tracking, HTTP logging interceptor, console overrides, environment-aware config, and daily rotating log files.

features.title: CLI Discoverability & DX
features.description: Includes `--help`, `--version`, and `--list-features` commands, plus curated ESLint/Prettier/Jest/env/request definition templates and Post-scaffold formatting.

technicalChallenges.title: Safe, idempotent-ish feature injection into existing NestJS apps
technicalChallenges.problem: Adding features to an existing project requires modifying files and installing dependencies without breaking unrelated user code, especially when only a subset of features is selected.
technicalChallenges.approach: Separated orchestration into focused modules (prompts, file copying, shell commands, and `main.ts` modifiers), validated target directories/Nest projects for `--add-feature`, and applied conditional template injection and dependency installation based on explicit user selections.

technicalChallenges.title: Composing Docker setups from modular service templates
technicalChallenges.problem: Generating a usable `docker-compose.yml` for different service combinations requires correct YAML composition, optional networking, and dependency ordering for the Node service.
technicalChallenges.approach: Built a Docker config generator that assembles service YAML snippets from template files, injects/removes network blocks as needed, validates custom network names, computes `depends_on` from selected backing services, and drops auxiliary files (Dockerfile/nginx.conf) when required.

technicalChallenges.title: Programmatically wiring selected capabilities into `main.ts`
technicalChallenges.problem: Users can choose different combinations of prefix/versioning, validation, security, Swagger, interceptors, and logging; the generated bootstrap code must remain coherent and correctly ordered.
technicalChallenges.approach: Implemented a `main-file.modifier` that conditionally inserts imports and runtime setup lines (including interceptor chaining and NestExpress/static asset configuration) and wraps bootstrap error handling, allowing feature-specific wiring without manual edits.

technicalChallenges.title: Balancing opinionated defaults with developer choice
technicalChallenges.problem: The CLI must provide production-friendly defaults while supporting different stacks (TypeORM vs Mongoose), package managers, and optional features across new and existing projects.
technicalChallenges.approach: Used an interactive prompt-driven flow with explicit feature toggles and per-feature template/dependency paths (pagination drivers, security selections, logger setup), plus documentation/changelog updates to keep behavior transparent across releases.

technicalChallenges.title: Maintaining template quality across evolving NestJS/tooling conventions
technicalChallenges.problem: Generated config and runtime integrations (linting, Swagger UI, logging, CORS/pagination behavior) needed refinement as the tool matured.
technicalChallenges.approach: Iterated through releases and maintenance commits to replace/update templates, improve Swagger UI assets, refactor pagination/Multer/logger setup, and fix runtime/config edge cases while preserving the CLI's additive workflow.

architecture.description: Nest Craft is structured as a Node.js CLI with a `bin/` command layer and a `lib/` implementation layer. The entrypoint performs a non-sudo guard and delegates to an argv manager that routes `init`, `--add-feature`, and informational commands. `init` and `add-feature` collect configuration through `@clack/prompts`-based modules, resolve/validate target paths, and orchestrate work via shell utilities (`execa`, `@nestjs/cli` for scaffolding, package installation) plus guard functions. Feature application is handled by `lib/files` (template copying, env/definition/config seeding, Swagger/logger/pagination/Multer/security asset injection, Prettier/Jest adjustments) and `main-file.modifier` (patching `src/main.ts` for global app wiring). Docker support is implemented in `lib/docker` by composing service YAML templates into a final `docker-compose.yml` and copying service-specific files. An architecture image prompt for generating a diagram is provided in `ARCHITECTURE_IMAGE_PROMPT.md` at the repository root.
